choices.text: Zinc is a transition metal because it sits in the d-block
Zinc is not a transition metal because Zn2+ has a completely filled 3d subshell
Zinc is a transition metal because it forms coloured complexes

questions.feedback: That trap reading is the one to unlearn: Zinc is a transition metal because it sits in the d-block. Reteach point: Zinc(II) has a full 3d subshell: no partially filled d orbitals, so zinc is not a transition metal.
questions.misconception: Zinc is a transition metal because it sits in the d-block.
questions.prompt: Which statement about zinc and transition metals is correct?

questions.answer: Sulphur has one paired 3p orbital; the repulsion between the paired electrons makes one of them easier to remove than an unpaired 3p electron in phosphorus, even though sulphur has the greater nuclear charge.
questions.feedback: The dip in scene s3 is an orbital effect, not a trend reversal: paired-electron repulsion in sulphur's 3p orbital outweighs the extra nuclear charge.
questions.prompt: The first ionisation energy dips from phosphorus to sulphur. Explain why, in one or two sentences.

choices.text: Nothing happens, because bromine is below iodine in group 17
The solution turns brown: bromine is a stronger oxidising agent than iodine, so it displaces iodide to form I2
The solution turns orange, because iodine displaces bromide

questions.feedback: Oxidising power falls down group 17 (scene s5): bromine sits above iodine, so bromine takes electrons from iodide and brown iodine forms.
questions.prompt: Bromine water is added to aqueous potassium iodide. What happens, and why?

questions.answer: The ammonia molecules act as ligands: each donates a lone pair to the Cu2+ ion, forming coordinate bonds and replacing the water ligands in a ligand-exchange reaction, giving the deep blue [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ complex.
questions.feedback: This is the crowding in scene s7: ligands donate lone pairs into the metal ion to form a complex, and a new ligand set means a new d-orbital split - and a new colour.
questions.prompt: Excess ammonia is added to aqueous copper(II) sulfate and the pale blue solution turns deep blue. Explain what the ammonia molecules do.
